chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) visited Salman al-Farisi (may God's mercy be upon him) during his illness.

And he said: O Salman! Verily, in your illness you have three characteristics: You are in a state of remembrance of God, the Mighty and Majestic; your supplication in it is accepted; and the illness does not leave upon you a sin except that it erases it.
May God grant you wellness until the expiration of your appointed time.

key_terms.أَجَل: Appointed time, term — one's destined time of death, as decreed by God
key_terms.خِصَال: Characteristics, traits, qualities — three positive spiritual qualities resulting from illness
key_terms.ذِكْر: Remembrance (of God) — being in a state of consciousness of the Divine, heightened during illness
key_terms.عَافِيَة: Wellness, good health, wholeness — a comprehensive term for physical and spiritual well-being
key_terms.عِلَّة: Illness, ailment — used here to denote the physical condition that brings spiritual benefits
key_terms.مُسْتَجَاب: Answered, accepted — the du'a of the sick person is more readily responded to by God

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the spiritual benefits of illness?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) visiting his loyal companion Salman al-Farisi during an illness in Medina. The Prophet offers profound consolation, teaching that illness is not merely a trial but carries three spiritual blessings: it places the believer in a state of divine remembrance, makes their prayers more likely to be accepted, and serves as an expiation for sins. The hadith culminates with a prophetic supplication for Salman's continued wellbeing, which the early Shia audience would have received as both theological reassurance and a model of the Prophet's compassion toward his companions.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. Muhammad b. Masrur (rh) narrated to us. He said: Al-Husayn b. Muhammad b. `Amer narrated to us from his uncle `Abdullah b. `Amer from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Aban b. `Uthman from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (s) visited Salman al-Farisi (rh) in his illness, so he said: O Salman! Surely, in your illness, you have three characteristics:
(1) You are in a state of remembering Allah, (2) your supplications in it are accepted, (3) the illness will not leave you until it causes your sins to fall.
May Allah gratify you with wellness until your time expires.
